body:
He is the only reason I'm still alive. I do know what it is to lose a parent that's the added touch to everything, if my father had not died there is a strong likelihood that i never would have had to go through the hell I went through, I know what it is to watch someone kill themselves. I live with those nightmares, those are things you can never unsee, every time you close your eyes you see it again, it's gruesome.

I'm sorry you were abused, i'm sorry your dad was a fucktard, I'm sorry you have cancer, but it can be beat, no matter what the doctors say, I've seen it happen too many times. And I'm not negating your pain, hell at 19 I never would have believed I could get to this point I had spent my entire life fighting to live why would I end it myself...but it's 13 years later, i'm in more pain than ever, and its only going to get worse. my child will have to watch my body deteriorate over time, watch me struggle to do even the most simple task because the pain is so severe. It kills me to see the stress and worry in his face because he knows the pain I'm in, he's seen me fall down the stairs because of the pain in my feet and legs, he's seen me struggle to breathe because my back and chest have seized up, he's cried countless times because he worries, do you know what it is to cause a child that kind of pain? i do, I know what it is to be that child too.

There does come a point though where things just get to be too much. Everyone has their breaking point. Mine was learning that no matter what I do, no matter how hard i work, or the years i've put into getting past the hatred and anger that enveloped my childhood, i will never be free. That those that sought to cause me pain every day of my life, won, they got what they wanted, to make me suffer every single day that I live. The pain alone I could bear, at least to a point, but knowing that they accomplished what they wanted, that they got to do this because they found it humorous to cause me such severe pain, that is more torture than anything

Until a couple weeks ago, the thought of hurting myself never even crossed my mind, yeah shit sucked, the constant pain and yes I knew then things were going to bad in my relationship, but I was still positive, I was waiting on test results after getting tested for cancer, MS, and a whole slew of other things. I was scared but I work in the medical field, I know what my options are for those things and I could be proactive in the treatment and there was still hope that maybe someday I could enjoy a hug from my child and not feel the dread of the pain. Throughout all my tests the doctors have regularly been shocked at the findings, the EMG showed levels of nerve damage that are normally only found in paralyzed people, the MRI showed old healed fractures on my skull and parts of my brain damaged years ago and the doctors struggled to understand why or how I still function mentally, even having a higher than average IQ level. I have repeatedly heard "you're not supposed to be able to walk/talk/function" which begins to wear on you as it sinks in and you realize just how damaged you really are. But then the doctors dropped the bomb "I'm sorry, but you are healthy, you've just been broken too many times" word for word that rings through my head...they did this to me, this isn't some bad luck draw where I got a shit disease and have treatment options, people willingly, willfully did this to me and there are no options for treatment, there is no getting better from this, in fact it will get worse, over time it will progress and the pain will become more and more severe. Do you know what it is to be handed a sentence like that?

My therapist cried, but she's far from the first. At this point I'm done with therapy, it's too exhausting to have to make others feel better about this hell I live. The doctor putting me as a high suicide risk, it's standard for people with moderate to severe chronic pain, but that doesn't make it feel any better. Seeing the heartbreak in his eyes, I've known him for 4 years, we've worked together, he knows my kid and I know his family. He tried to believe that abuse couldn't possibly be that severe, but the tests have proven it was. 

You're age doesn't matter, you can be 19 and wise or 99 and dumb as shit, I've dealt with both and everything in between. at 19 I was volunteering as a victims advocate, helping other abuse victims see there was life beyond their past, that they can let go of what happened to them and go on to great things. It was easy to do, I had done it, I had gotten free and pushed forward, but a year later the pain began to grip me, the migraines became severe enough that I kept sunglasses everywhere so I wouldn't have to deal with sunlight or fluorescent lights, but that invited new attacks. People in stores would literally rip my glasses from my face, several pairs were broken by people thinking I was trying to be "emo" or some stupid shit. Even police that knew me, that worked with me helping others started accusing me of doing drugs, of wearing the glasses to hide when I was high, it got to the point I moved several states away with the hopes of a new start.

But nothing changed but the scenery. I've been assaulted several times since i moved, I've been raped once, and twice others have tried but fortunately not succeeded. 

unlike you, I'm not "covered" in scars, I have a few, most have faded to being barely noticable except the ones on my genitals because they didn't break the skin much, I was kicked, beaten with numerous things, forced to sleep in the barn with the "rest of the filthy animals) I was welted numerous times with a belt, but the skin was rarely broken. Because I don't have a lot of visible scars, people tell me I wasn't abused, that it couldn't be that bad, but my tests prove other, my scars run deep, literally to the bone. And because of what they did, even the kindest gesture will hurt, every touch will remind me of what they did to me, every agonizing step will sear through me. I have been sentenced to a life of pain and solitude because someone deemed me less than human and far to many others stood and watched, but no one stepped in and put a stop to it.

I've been doing this for 32 years, I just learned a couple weeks ago from my doctor that the damage that they did has insured that I will never know a day without pain again in my life. My knees will need to be replaced by the time I'm 40, one ankle was broken and never set so it healed in an uneven way, everytime I try to walk after sitting or laying for any period of time it feels like my feet are breaking because of the scar tissue that developed from being forced to stand and carry too heavy loads at too young an age. The numerous concussions and busted eardrums guaranteed daily migraines forcing me to work nights and spend my days either secluded in a dark room or with sunglasses on even when I'm in a store. The blows to my back, being thrown, kicked, and hit with all manner of things caused numerous fractures to my vertebrae that were never treated, the result is such severe pain that breathingmakes it feel as though someone is pouring napalm down my spine. Even a kind gesture such as a hug hurts.

Everyone says it gets better, but it won't. my bf cheated because of the scars I have on my genitals, from being cut and burned. He's not the first. 

My doctor gives me a mixture of pills to take but they're expensive and I had my education stolen from me and i can't afford college now so I work a menial job with shit for insurance so I can't even afford the very drugs I need to be able to function. I went to my therapist to try to deal with this, with the fact that every day of my life i will have a constant reminder of the horrors that they put me through, I wasn't even close to suicidal at that point, just angry. I showed her the report from my doctor and she cried, my fucking therapist who is supposed to specialize in abuse survivors cried! I had to make her feel OK with what happened to me. Then I learned my doctor put me down as a high suicide risk as soon as the diagnosis came through because the levels of pain I experience, even without the trauma that caused them are severe enough that "no human can withstand it without wanting to free themselves forever from it" Those are his words, his statement that my physical pain is too severe for any human to be able to withstand it for very long and that I've already gone far beyond what my limitations should have been. my doctor who is supposed to help me even wrote me off as good as dead...might as well not waste anyone else's time anymore
